newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan seen buying U.S. pork through Aug shipments.
newsitem.headline: Japan seen buying U.S. pork through Aug shipments.

text.p: Japan is expected to buy U.S. pork actively at least until August shipments, due to Tokyo's lifting of an emergency tariff on July 1 and a drop in domestic pork production this summer, traders said on Friday.
On Thursday, CME pork belly futures closed up by the three cent a lb daily limit in the key August contract, boosted by talk of Japanese buying interest, according to floor traders.

"It's not surprising that Japanese importers are starting to buy U.S. pork now, if we look at low domestic stocks, a lack of Taiwanese pork and declining domestic supplies," a pork trader at a major Japanese trade house said.
"I expect Japanese buying is likely to continue at least until August," another pork trader in Tokyo said.
Pork stocks in Japan totalled 117,308 tonnes at the end of May, down 41 percent from a year earlier, according to the Agriculture and Livestock Industries Corp.
Stock figures for individual pork products, such as pork bellies, were not available.
The Japanese government on July 1 lifted an emergency import tariff on pork that had been put in place on April 1 to limit the influx of foreign pork.

"Local importers usually begin active buying immediately after a tariff is lifted, and they did so this time," the second pork trader said. "No Taiwanese pork is available now and we have no choice but to cover our needs with U.S. pork."
In March, Japan banned all pork imports from Taiwan after an outbreak of the highly contagious foot-and-mouth disease.

Traders also said that domestic pork supplies have been declining, partly due to torrential rains earlier this month that caused landslides and flash flooding on the southern island of Kyushu, a major Japanese pork-producing region.
Pork supplies from Kyushu slowed following the rains, traders said.
